facts_of_case: The husband sued for divorce on the ground that the wife is guilty of adulterous course of life. The wife denied the allegation and attributed it to lack of mental equilibrium of the husband.

legal_principles.principle: Marriages are made in heaven, but this one has turned into a hell for sure.
legal_principles.held: The allegations and the counter allegations are indicative of the intense hatred and rancour between the parties.
cited_cases: V. Bhagat vs D. Bhagat on 19 November, 1993
use_in: divorce cases with allegations of cruelty

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.
legal_principles.held: Notwithstanding the dismissal of a similar application by the Delhi High Court and the dismissal of a special leave petition there against by this Court, this is a fit and proper case and this is the most appropriate stage at which the petitioner should be granted divorce on the ground of cruelty.
use_in: divorce cases with allegations of irretrievable breakdown

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the appeal and granted divorce on the ground of mental cruelty.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea
use_for_drafting: responding to allegations of adultery and mental cruelty
